title: ARTISTS FUTURES: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICES II
description: Dives into the wide range of professionalism for artists within and adjacent to the art world. The class provides students the necessary skills to advance their work as emerging artists, addressing portfolio preparation and artist opportunities like graduate education, exhibitions, residencies, and grants. Also introduces students to the wide variety of careers available to artists and provides them with building blocks to move forward within these careers. Guest speakers illuminate opportunities in several fields including curatorial practice, design, marketing, art business, education, and non-profit work.
prerequisites_raw: Must be in upper division standing.

title: Art Since 1950
description: Developments in American and European art since 1950 with an emphasis on the most recent decades. Focus ranges from the post-war impact of the New York School, Pop Art, Minimalism and Conceptualism to more recent, postmodern trends.

title: Introduction to Contemporary Theory
description: A basic beginning survey of contemporary art, film and media theory, focusing specifically on: realism, formalism, semiotics, phenomenology, psychoanalysis, feminism, Marxism, gender/queer studies, poststructuralism, post-colonial theory and broader issues of authorship, narratology, postmodernism, and multiculturalism.

title: Visual Arts as Culture
description: Exploration of visual arts and culture, including the evolving social and practical parameters of technologically produced images and the shifting arenas of ideology, analysis, and criticism.

title: Digital Video
description: The making and use of video in contemporary art. Hands-on production and post production are combined with viewing, critique, and discussion topics, including cultural prominence and future trends. Single and multiple channel, installation, and integration with other media are all encouraged.

title: Memory: An Interdisciplinary Exploration
description: Introduces students to the trans-disciplinary fields of memory and migration through interdisciplinary collaboration. Course responsibilities include class participation, a midterm essay and a final interdisciplinary project. This course draws upon the connections between neuroscience, arts and studies of human migration.

title: Memory: An Interdisciplinary Exploration

Course responsibilities include class participation, a midterm essay and a final interdisciplinary project. This course draws upon the connections between neuroscience, arts and studies of human migration.

title: Performance
description: A workshop introduction to the forms, styles, and strategies of contemporary performance art, which may involve the use of the body, space, narrative, audience, object, installation, and multimedia.

title: Performance & Environment
description: This workshop introduces students to artists in the field of environmental and ecological activism. Students develop projects that address environmental justice, landscape and place using performance, video, installation and other conceptual strategies.
prerequisites_raw: OR Upper Division OR Instructor Approval

title: Personal Narrative
description: Intensive writing-based workshop designed for formulating and producing artwork based on one's own personal experiences and histories. Experimentation and expansion into other artistic media are encouraged.

title: Spoken Word
description: A workshop introduction to the use of voice as an artistic medium, with emphasis on personal monologue, and improvisation.

title: Art and Science of Aerospace Culture
description: Interdisciplinary course/seminar/practice that explores technological, aesthetic, cultural, and political aspects of the space side of the aerospace complex. Design history,space complex aesthetics, cinema intersections, imaging/telecommunications, human spaceflight history, reduced/alternating gravity experimentation, space systems design/utilization.

title: Mediatechnology
description: Telegraph, telephone, phonograph, and film techniques that have engendered new forms of representation, communications, and thinking. Course studies the impact of these transformations in literature and on literature. Taught in English.

title: Special Topics in Art
description: Related to Art 1C Thursday colloquium guest artists, focusing on activism through art. Tuesday we will explore the practical side of how to create projects that go beyond the gallery and focus on changing public policy through art, advocacy, social media, interventions, graphics, photography, documentation, sculpture and raw passion.
